KO.rationale: Coca-Cola exhibits best-in-class profitability (62%+ gross margin, 34% operating margin, 40.4% ROE) and a dominant global franchise, but the stock is quantitatively unattractive at current levels. The P/E has expanded ~5.7 turns from the Sep 2025 trough (23.5x) to 29.2x today while net margin and ROE have remained flat at 0.259 and 0.404 respectively — the market is paying significantly more for the same profitability. The stock sits at the extreme of its own valuation range (29.2x vs. 23.2x–29.6x window), the 3.4% earnings yield falls below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.45%, and the Baa corporate bond yield of 6.0% makes the equity offer less cash-flow yield than investment-grade debt. The fundamental case for the premium rests on only two quarters of data with no year-over-year confirmation, and Q1 operating cash flow was negative $5.20B. The IRS transfer-pricing dispute carries a potential liability near $14B, disclosed and unresolved. The 2026 FIFA World Cup catalyst (projected 278M case uplift per BofA) and India bottler IPO plan provide modest near-term support, but these are insufficient to offset the stretched valuation. A reversion to the median observed P/E of ~26x would imply ~11% downside. The risk/reward skews negatively from a fundamental-valuation standpoint.
